title: 1950 AHSME Problem 43
statement: The sum to infinity of \(\dfrac17+\dfrac{2}{7^2}+\dfrac{1}{7^3}+\dfrac{2}{7^4}+\cdots\) is:

solutions.text:
Grouping consecutive terms gives a geometric series whose first grouped term is \[ \frac17+\frac2{49}=\frac9{49} \] and whose ratio is \(\tfrac1{49}.\) Hence the sum is \[ \frac{\frac9{49}}{1-\frac1{49}} =\frac9{48} =\frac3{16}. \] This is not among choices A through D.

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Group the series into consecutive pairs of terms
Each pair is \(\frac{1}{49}\) times the preceding pair
